newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers in talks to avoid Mar 5 strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers in talks to avoid Mar 5 strike.

text.p: Unions at the Brazilian port of Paranagua are negotiating with authorities to avert a planned March 5 strike, the National Portworkers Federation said.
The Federation added that if these talks fail, the work stoppage will likely spread to other ports.
"They are trying to come to an understanding," said secretary-general Jose Renato de Rosa. "If they don't agree, then there is the possibility of a strike."
Paranagua portworkers are demanding a 21 percent wage increase which was awarded to all Brazilian portworkers in March 1996 but which they have so far not received, de Rosa said.
If negotiations with port authorities fail, Paranagua workers will go on strike for 24 hours on March 5.
Paranagua port officials and unions were not immediately available to comment on the progress of talks.
De Rosa stressed that other Brazilian ports would only join the strike out of sympathy for their colleagues at Paranagua and had no wage demands of their own.
"The question at stake is a wage readjustment of 21 percent which was not passed on to our companions at Paranagua last March," he said.
A national strike was due to start on March 6 if the Paranagua wage talks failed but the duration of the possible nationwide stoppage had still not been decided, de Rosa said.
